# If This Was a Movie

## Lead

If This Was a Movie is a song by American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift, first released as a bonus track on the Target-exclusive deluxe edition of her third studio album, Speak Now (2010), through Big Machine Records. It was co-written by Swift and Martin Johnson and produced by Swift with Nathan Chapman. Issued digitally in November 2011, the song debuted at number 10 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and reached number 3 on Digital Songs with 162,000 downloads in its first week. Critics at Billboard characterized it as a fast-paced pop rock ballad that signaled a maturing lyrical perspective for Swift. Swift released If This Was a Movie (Taylor’s Version) on March 17, 2023, as part of her re-recording project timed to the start of the Eras Tour; the new version topped the US Country Digital Song Sales chart and reached number 4 on Digital Song Sales. The re-recording was later included on the streaming compilation The More Fearless (Taylor’s Version) Chapter. The title has been used for other recordings by independent artists, but the Swift composition is the widely covered work under this name in mainstream music media and charts. , , , , , , , , , , , , 

## Background and writing

The song was written by Taylor Swift and Martin Johnson, the latter known as the frontman of Boys Like Girls, and produced by Swift with Nathan Chapman. Billboard’s track review credits list Swift and Johnson as the songwriters and Chapman and Swift as the producers, with the release under Big Machine. These credits align with the broader production approach of the Speak Now era, in which Swift worked extensively with Chapman. 

Swift originally placed If This Was a Movie on the Target-exclusive deluxe edition of Speak Now, released on October 25, 2010. The album marked a period when Swift emphasized authorial control over her work; the track represents one of her few co-written pieces in the Speak Now era. , 

## Composition and lyrics

Billboard described If This Was a Movie as a fast-paced ballad propelled by a recurring guitar figure and a dramatic chorus with layered harmonies that complement Swift’s country-pop vocal timbre. The review highlighted the song’s narrative of longing and imagined reconciliation after a breakup, reading it as a coming-of-age moment that moves beyond high school fantasy to more adult themes. 

## Release and versions

- Original release: If This Was a Movie first appeared on the Target-exclusive deluxe edition of Speak Now (released October 25, 2010). The original recording is credited to Big Machine Records. , 
- Digital release as part of deluxe tracks: On November 8, 2011, six deluxe tracks from Speak Now—including If This Was a Movie—were released digitally, which led to the song’s entry on multiple charts. 
- Re-recording (Taylor’s Version): Swift released If This Was a Movie (Taylor’s Version) on March 17, 2023, as one of four surprise tracks timed to the start of The Eras Tour. The single’s product page lists “℗ 2023 Taylor Swift.” Swift later grouped the track within The More Fearless (Taylor’s Version) Chapter on streaming services. , , , 

Commentary around the re-recording’s placement noted that Swift emphasized Speak Now as “completely self-written” when announcing its re-recorded version, while If This Was a Movie is co-written with Martin Johnson. Media reporting framed fan expectations that the track would be released separately from Speak Now (Taylor’s Version) and associated with the Fearless era compilations on streaming. 

## Critical reception

Billboard’s track review viewed If This Was a Movie as evidence of Swift’s lyrical maturation and stronger age-appropriate themes, while praising its arrangement as a streamlined, fast-paced ballad with a memorable chorus and supporting harmonies. The outlet also noted the song’s impact a year after Speak Now’s release, underscoring its late surge due to the digital release of deluxe tracks. 

## Commercial performance

Original (2011):
- US Billboard Hot 100: debuted at number 10 (week of November 26, 2011), the highest-ranking debut that week. 
- Digital Songs (US): debuted at number 3 with 162,000 downloads; it also led the Country Digital Song Sales tally for a week in November 2011. 
- Canadian Hot 100: entered at number 17 amid a wave of Speak Now-related tracks reaching Canada charts. 

Taylor’s Version (2023):
- US Digital Song Sales: debuted at number 4 with 11,300 sold (charts dated April 1, 2023). 
- US Country Digital Song Sales: debuted at number 1. Billboard noted the composition became the first to top the Country Digital Song Sales chart via two different versions, and the result extended Swift’s record number of leaders on the tally. 
- United Kingdom: appeared on the Official Singles Chart update and ranked on the Official Singles Sales Chart and Official Singles Downloads Chart; it also entered the Official Trending Chart. , 

Swift’s pattern of high Hot 100 debuts was emphasized by Billboard in a separate year-end feature, which referenced If This Was a Movie’s top 10 start. 

## Live performances

Swift performed If This Was a Movie as a surprise song during The Eras Tour on June 23, 2023, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, playing it on piano as part of the acoustic segment of the show. Billboard’s compiled list documents the performance date and context within the tour’s rotating surprise songs. 

## Credits and personnel

Original version (2010):
- Songwriters: Taylor Swift, Martin Johnson. 
- Producers: Nathan Chapman, Taylor Swift. 
- Label/imprint: Big Machine Records; the original audio release is credited “℗ 2010 Big Machine Records, LLC.” 
- Album context: Speak Now (Target-exclusive deluxe edition). 

Taylor’s Version (2023):
- Performer: Taylor Swift. 
- Release: single issued March 17, 2023; included on The More Fearless (Taylor’s Version) Chapter. , , 
- Producer credit: streaming service metadata lists production credits for the Taylor’s Version; platform credits are viewable on TIDAL. 

## Charts and certifications

Selected chart peaks:
- US Billboard Hot 100 (original): number 10 (week of November 26, 2011). 
- US Digital Songs (original): number 3 (162,000 downloads, week of November 26, 2011). 
- US Country Digital Song Sales (original): number 1 (one week in November 2011). 
- Canadian Hot 100 (original): number 17. 
- US Digital Song Sales (Taylor’s Version): number 4 (11,300 downloads, charts dated April 1, 2023). 
- US Country Digital Song Sales (Taylor’s Version): number 1. 
- UK Official Singles charts (Taylor’s Version): entries on Official Singles Chart update, Official Singles Downloads Chart, and Official Singles Sales Chart; appeared on Official Trending Chart. , 

No certifications from the RIAA were identified in the organization’s public Gold & Platinum database for this song or its re-recording as of the reported dates; chart performance and sales/streaming figures above derive from Billboard and Official Charts reporting. , , , , 

## Other uses of the title

Other recordings have used the title If This Was a Movie, but chart and mainstream media documentation predominantly refer to Swift’s composition. This article covers the Taylor Swift work and its re-recording because it is the song with significant coverage in major outlets and chart authorities. , , 

## Controversies and notable discussions

In the lead-up to Speak Now (Taylor’s Version), UK outlet Capital FM reported fan commentary that Swift’s emphasis on the album being “completely self-written” would preclude the inclusion of If This Was a Movie—which is co-written with Martin Johnson—on the re-recorded track list. The song was instead released earlier as a stand-alone Taylor’s Version single and grouped with The More Fearless (Taylor’s Version) Chapter on streaming. These discussions reflect the public narrative around Swift’s catalog control and the framing of her re-recordings. , ,

The Taylor Swift Song That Won’t Be On 'Speak Now (Taylor’s Version)'
=====================================================================

9 May 2023, 15:27

![Image 3: Taylor Swift could be leaving a song off 'Speak Now'](https://imgs.capitalfm.com/images/577486?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=naLFerK3WbUXcJ6eisIJzJ7bkF0=)

Taylor Swift could be leaving a song off 'Speak Now'. Picture: Getty/Taylor Swift/Twitter

[![Image 4: Facebook share](https://www.capitalfm.com/assets_v4r/gusto/img/facebook-share.png)](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?href=www.capitalfm.com%2Fnews%2Ftaylor-swift-speak-now-if-this-was-a-movie%2F&app_id=184899318222048)

By Savannah Roberts

Here's why fans think 'If This Was A Movie' won't be on 'Speak Now (Taylor's Version)'...

#### Listen to this article

Loading audio...

It’s _finally_ official, [Taylor Swift](https://www.capitalfm.com/artists/taylor-swift/) has confirmed what fans have been theorising for months (and months) – ['Speak Now (Taylor's Version)'](https://www.capitalfm.com/artists/taylor-swift/speak-now-taylors-version-release-date/) is coming!

The pop powerhouse set hearts racing when she announced live in concert that her third studio album was the next in line to get a re-release; dropping July 7.

[**Which Albums Is Taylor Swift Re-Recording? A Guide To Her First Six Albums**](https://www.capitalfm.com/news/taylor-swift-albums-rerecording-songs/)

[**Every Single Outfit Taylor Swift Wears On The Eras Tour**](https://www.capitalfm.com/features/taylor-swifts-eras-tour-outfits/)

The ‘Midnights’ songstress revealed that the new version of her third studio album, originally released in 2010, will be 22 tracks long – but it looks like 'If This Was A Movie' might not be on the record.

Here's why the original 'Speak Now' bonus track might be left off the 2023 edition...

![Image 5](https://cf-images.eu-west-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6057949401001/c51fd59f-7ee9-485a-b219-820b9c05b16f/a8f22e22-ab13-4c92-9d8c-0dbc0f58da8f/640x360/match/image.jpg)

Taylor Swift dives into the stage

![Image 6: The 'Speak Now' tracklist theory explained](https://imgs.capitalfm.com/images/577483?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=BZ_oFcYJiuTHX7ewKWHvUv7bYy4=)

The 'Speak Now' tracklist theory explained. Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/1488050242)

**Will 'If This Was a Movie' be on 'Speak Now (Taylor's Version)?**
-------------------------------------------------------------------

Back in March, [Taylor dropped four songs to celebrate the beginning of The Eras Tour](https://www.capitalfm.com/news/taylor-swift-new-songs-eras-tour/), one of which was 'If This Was a Movie', giving us our first taste of 'Speak Now (Taylor's Version)' – or so we thought.

However, fans were confused that the track was added to the end of 'Fearless (Taylor's Version)' on streaming services upon its release.

'If This Was a Movie' was track 16 on 'Speak Now's deluxe edition but more importantly, it was the only song that wasn't written solely by Taylor, interesting!

The pop star spoke about the lack of co-writers on the album in her announcement tweet: "I first made Speak Now, completely self-written, between the ages of 18 and 20."

> speak now tv will have 22 songs (6 are vault tracks, 16 were already released). ‘if this was a movie’ is not be part of the album, and sntv will be PURELY self written 💜 [pic.twitter.com/gEFOz6dFnp](https://t.co/gEFOz6dFnp)
> 
> — kat (@midnightsjieun) [May 6, 2023](https://twitter.com/midnightsjieun/status/1654697740549627905?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> Taylor said that Speak Now (Taylor's Version) consists of 22 songs, 6 of which are from the vault. That us leaves with 16 songs from the og SN. So were getting Mine-Superman without If This Was a Movie and the Acoustic Versions of Back to December and Haunted (and ofc "US" ver) [pic.twitter.com/ycKvGyhD3J](https://t.co/ycKvGyhD3J)
> 
> — dimitris (@ofdimitris) [May 6, 2023](https://twitter.com/ofdimitris/status/1654816104534151168?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

It didn't take long for fans to come to the conclusion that the song in question was omitted from the the re-recording so it could remain completely self-written, just as the non-deluxe edition was.

There will be six never-heard-before songs from Taylor's Vault, she revealed in her tweet: "With six extra songs I’ve sprung loose from the vault, I absolutely cannot wait to celebrate Speak Now (Taylor’s Version) with you on July 7th."

One Swiftie tweeted about the singer's decision to not include any co-writers: "speak now tv will have 22 songs (6 are vault tracks, 16 were already released). ‘if this was a movie’ is not be part of the album, and sntv will be PURELY self written \[sic\]."

Another fan guessed what the extra tracks would be, they wrote: "So were getting Mine-Superman without If This Was a Movie and the Acoustic Versions of Back to December and Haunted."

**Why was 'Speak Now' completely self-written?**
------------------------------------------------

Taylor revealed in an interview with [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/taylor-swift-rolling-stone-interview-880794/) in 2019 that she decided to make herself the sole writer on her third record in response to critics.

She said: "When I was 18, they were like, 'She doesn’t really write those songs.' So my third album I wrote by myself as a reaction to that."

Rihanna Still Atop Hot 100, Taylor Swift's 'Movie' Premieres in Top 10

[Rihanna](https://www.billboard.com/artist/rihanna/658897) collects a third week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with “We Found Love” (featuring Calvin Harris), while [Taylor Swift](https://www.billboard.com/artist/taylor-swift/766101) bookends the top 10 with a record-extending debut.

“Found,” the lead single from Rihanna’s sixth studio album, “Talk That Talk,” due Monday (Nov. 21), spends a third week at No. 1 on the Digital Songs chart with 227,000 downloads sold, down 4%, according to Nielsen SoundScan. On Radio Songs, the dance track lifts 4-3 with 115 million all-format audience impressions, up 12%, according to Nielsen BDS.

Further helping set up the album’s launch, second single “You Da One” debuts on the Hot 100 at No. 73 and Radio Songs at No. 28 with 38 million in first-week audience after the song was serviced to radio Friday (11). The bow on the latter list is the highest since [Lady Gaga](https://www.billboard.com/artist/lady-gaga/1003999)‘s “Born This Way” roared in at No. 6 the week of Feb. 26, 2011.

At the opposite end of the Hot 100’s top tier, Taylor Swift debuts with “If This Was a Movie” (No. 10). On Digital Songs, the song starts at No. 3 with 162,000 downloads sold. Swift also arrives at Nos. 13 and 26 on the Hot 100 with “Ours” (148,000; her next country radio single) and “Superman” (91,000), respectively.

ADVERTISEMENT

[**CMA Awards: Taylor Swift Reclaims Top Prize**](https://www.billboard.com/column/the-615/cma-awards-taylor-swift-reclaims-top-prize-1005501552.story)

The tracks made their digital retail debuts Nov. 8, after previously being available only on the deluxe CD version of Swift’s “Speak Now” album at Target stores. Six bonus “Speak” tracks made their arrivals digitally last week, with the Hot 100-debuting trio of tracks joined by alternate versions of “Speak” songs “Mine,” “Back to December” and “Haunted,” the latter of which re-enters the Hot 100 at No. 98 (24,000).

“Movie” marks Swift’s Hot 100-record-extending eighth title to debut in the top 10. [Lil Wayne](https://www.billboard.com/artist/lil-wayne/352101) ranks second with six top 10 launches. “Movie” is Swift’s 10th top 10 overall and her first since “December” (No. 6) last year.

With her Hot 100 entrances, Swift continues her run of accumulating accolades. Last Wednesday (9), she was named the CMA’s Entertainer of the Year, while Monday (14), Billboard reported that “Speak” single “Sparks Fly” became her fifth No. 1 on the Country Songs chart. And, she’s not done yet: the 21-year-old will receive Billboard’s Woman of the Year award at the 2011 Billboard Women in Music event Dec. 2.

Below Rihanna’s reigning Hot 100 leader, [LMFAO](https://www.billboard.com/artist/lmfao/1054925)‘s “Sexy and I Know It” logs a second week at No. 2. The cut remains at No. 2 on Digital Songs (195,000, down 4%), while slipping 5-6 on Radio Songs, although with a 6% audience gain to 98 million.

[Adele](https://www.billboard.com/artist/adele/810846)‘s former five-week No. 1 “Someone Like You” holds at No. 3 on the Hot 100. The song descends 1-2 on Radio Songs (128 million all-format audience impressions, down 11%) and 3-6 on Digital Songs (143,000, down 1%).

“Someone” has received two high-profile TV tributes since last week: NBC’s “Saturday Night Live” good-naturedly ribbed the song’s dramatic lyrics (with even [Coldplay](https://www.billboard.com/artist/coldplay/401639) unable to hold back the tears upon hearing it), while Fox’s “Glee” last night blended the ballad with fellow Adele song “Rumour Has It”; the mash-up is currently the top-selling title in the iTunes Store, likely setting up the “Glee” cast’s best debut and rank for any of its releases this season on next week’s Hot 100.

[David Guetta](https://www.billboard.com/artist/david-guetta/527799)‘s “Without You,” featuring [Usher](https://www.billboard.com/artist/usher/36758), climbs 6-4 with the Hot 100’s Digital Gainer tag (162,000, up 32%). With the boost, Guetta achieves his highest career Hot 100 placement; he had previously risen as high as No. 5 with “Sexy Chick,” featuring [Akon](https://www.billboard.com/artist/akon/491541), last year.

Rounding out the Hot 100’s top five, former four-week No. 1 “Moves Like Jagger” by [Maroon 5](https://www.billboard.com/artist/maroon-5/486079) featuring [Christina Aguilera](https://www.billboard.com/artist/christina-aguilera/325726) drops 4-5. [Gym Class Heroes](https://www.billboard.com/artist/gym-class-heroes/647857)‘ “Stereo Hearts,” featuring Maroon 5’s Adam Levine, dips 5-6 on the Hot 100 and [Foster the People](https://www.billboard.com/artist/foster-the-people/1530525)‘s “Pumped Up Kicks” holds at No. 7.

[Flo Rida](https://www.billboard.com/artist/flo-rida/873165)‘s “Good Feeling” maintains its No. 8 Hot 100 ranking and [Bruno Mars](https://www.billboard.com/artist/bruno-mars/1054629) enters the top 10 with “It Will Rain” (12-9). The track from the “Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1” soundtrack climbs 10-8 on Digital Songs (130,000, up 34%) and 22-19 on Radio Songs (50 million, up 12%) to become Mars’ eighth Hot 100 top 10 dating to his arrival less than two years ago as a guest on B.o.B’s two-week No. 1 “Nothin’ On You.”

Is our little princess growing up? “If This Was a Movie,” a new single off the deluxe edition of [Taylor Swift](https://www.billboard.com/artist/taylor-swift/766101)‘s “Speak Now,” made a splash on the Hot 100 a year after the singer’s third album was originally released. The fast-paced ballad suggests that the 21-year-old has been through a breakup and wishes to reverse it: “I just want it back the way it was before/And I just wanna see you back at my front door,” she sings. Swift is lyrically coming of age, abandoning the fantasy world of high school and exploring more mature content. A simple recurring guitar riff moves the song along, and its dramatic chorus features simple harmonies providing sbackup to Swift’s signature twang. She may not be entering [Christina Aguilera](https://www.billboard.com/artist/christina-aguilera/325726)‘s “Dirrty” phase quite just yet, but “If This Was a Movie” represents a more age-appropriate track for the innocent country hero.

Taylor Swift to surprise release 4 previously unheard songs tonight to celebrate beginning of The Eras Tour
===========================================================================================================

That's one way to celebrate!

* * *

Taylor Swift will drop four new songs tonight as a special surprise to mark the beginning of The Eras Tour.

Marking the news on her Instagram Stories, Taylor revealed that all of the songs have been previously unreleased...until now.

Dropping at midnight tonight (or 5am GMT if you're in the UK!), the songs will be Eyes Open (Taylor's Version), Safe & Sound featuring Joy Williams and John Paul White (Taylor's Version), If This Was A Movie (Taylor's Version) and All The Girls You Loved Before.

In terms of the history of these songs - Eyes Open was a song Taylor previously recorded for the soundtrack of the first Hunger Games film, as was Safe & Sound. Safe & Sound was originally a duet with duo The Civil Wars. They have since broken up, but Taylor has got the team back together with the duo - Joy Williams and John Paul White - now being credited under their solo monikers.

#### MORE: [Taylor Swift's Official Charts history in full](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/5387/taylor-swift/)

If This Was A Movie is taken from the deluxe edition of Taylor's third LP Speak Now, while All The Girls You Loved Before is a song that hasn't been officially released before now, thought to be taken from recording sessions from Lover and produced by Joel Little (Lorde, Marina).

Taylor's first major tour since 2017's reputation, The Eras Tour will for the first time encompass all of Taylor's discography, from her self-titled debut to last year's blockbuster Midnights.

[The Eras Tour is set to kick off Stateside in Glendale, Arizona on March 17](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/taylor-swift-announces-the-eras-tour-first-major-tour-in-over-five-years__37721/), where the city has been temporarily renamed Swift City in Tay's honour. She'll be supported on the opening night by Paramore and GAYLE.

As for the much-anticipated setlist of the tour, that's yet to arrive - although some fans definitely think they've cracked some of the songs we can expect to be performed ([Style, please!](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/gracie-abrams-talks-aching-debut-album-good-riddance-and-touring-with-taylor-swift-working-through-these-feelings-in-real-time-was-cathartic__38667/)).

[See Taylor Swift's The Eras Tour setlist in full here](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/taylor-swift-eras-tour-setlist-2023-in-full-what-songs-will-taylor-sing-at-stadium-concerts-across-america-what-time-is-she-on-stage-and-who-are-support-acts-paramore-haim-and-more__38772/).

[Artists](https://www.officialcharts.com/artists/) Taylor Swift tops Official Trending Chart with All Of The Girls You Loved Before ================================================================================ The song originally missed the cut for Lover, but was released as a surprise for fans last week. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ![Image 10: Taylor Swift](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2023-06/Taylor%20Swift%20Cruel%20Summer.png?itok=S5qh3GyS) By George Griffiths | 21 March 2023 share:[Share on Facebook![Image 11: Share on Facebook](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/40591d706d1c3f2a82207b6b11a09bb6)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on Twitter![Image 12: Share on Twitter](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/5319b25504889176c307a6802ff90863)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on WhatsApp![Image 13: Share on WhatsApp](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/3dbabd8b9a7cb58cdee80998d3a65943)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on LinkedIn![Image 14: Share on LinkedIn](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/9a30dee02fa1cc5b025bf509a34a8a06)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share on Reddit![Image 15: Share on Reddit](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/b9248b221d651bf490de48c5b78c8ba2)](javascript:void\(0\))[Share via Email![Image 16: Share via email](blob:https://www.officialcharts.com/87c9a2b43250ffff6987a6c4b94171c6)](javascript:void\(0\)) * * * Taylor Swift tops this week's Official Trending Chart with All Of The Girls You Loved Before. Originally recorded for inclusion in 2019's Lover album, the track didn't make the cut (it shares a lot of sentiment and sonic similarities with the title track, which may have tipped it off the edge) but was recently [surprised released as a gift to fans following the start of The Eras Tour, alongside three other songs](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/taylor-swift-to-surprise-release-4-previously-unheard-songs-tonight-to-celebrate-beginning-of-the-eras-tour__38802/) yes Open (Taylor's Version), Safe & Sound featuring Joy Williams and John Paul White (Taylor's Version) and If This Was A Movie (Taylor's Version), which also debuts on the Official Trending Chart today. All Of The Girls You Loved Before is currently bracing itself for a Top 10 debut at Number 7. It would become her 22nd UK Top 10 overall, and first of the year, following [Anti-Hero (1), Lavender Haze (3) and Snow On The Beach featuring Lana Del Rey (4) last year](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/5387/taylor-swift/). LISTEN to the Official Trending Chart here: ------------------------------------------- Other new entries on the Official Trending Chart this week include BTS member Jimin (Set Me Free - Pt 2), Irish singer-songwriter Hozier (Eat Your Young) and Lewis Capaldi with his emotional new track, taken from his forthcoming Netflix documentary of the same name (How I'm Feeling Now). As for the high risers, three tracks looks srt to break into the Top 40 this week - Meghan Trainor's kitsch follow up to viral sensation Made You Look (Mother), Tom Grennan's latest (Here) and Zara Larsson's high-tempo pop anthem (Can't Tame Her). [Español](https://www.billboard.com/lists/taylor-swift-todas-las-canciones-sorpresa-the-eras-tour-2023/)

[Taylor Swift](https://www.billboard.com/artist/taylor-swift/)‘s Eras Tour set list features two surprise songs (or mashups) performed during a mini acoustic set, on each date of the the superstar’s trek, which kicked off in March 2023.

Guitar in hand and making her way to the end of the stage’s catwalk at March 17’s Eras kickoff in Glendale, Ariz., Swift revealed her intentions for the acoustic portion of her long-awaited live show. She’ll perform a surprise song that will not be played again on this tour — probably.

“The plan, the goal, would be to play different songs every single night and never repeat one. Right? So that when you heard one on this tour, you would know it’s the only time that I was going to play it in the acoustic set, unless — caveat — unless I mess it up so badly,” she said with a small laugh, “that I have to do it over again in some other city. Send your best wishes towards me that I don’t do that.”

The Eras Tour is her first real tour in five years, and the first time the prolific songwriter is getting to perform selections from _Lover_, _Folklore_, _Evermore_, _Midnights_ and _The Tortured Poets Department_ to sold-out stadium crowds.

[Eras Tour night one](https://www.billboard.com/lists/taylor-swifts-eras-tour-best-moments-review/) introduced a career-spanning, whopping [44-song setlist](https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/taylor-swifts-eras-tour-first-show-1235289197/) with a runtime of more than three hours, with Swift playing anywhere from one to eight tracks from all 10 of her full-length studio albums. The show’s nightly surprise is sure to keep her fans on their tallest tiptoes, waiting to hear what gem will be unveiled at their concert.

The only city that was unable to get a surprise set is Vienna, Austria, where Swift was scheduled to perform from August 8 to 10 before the shows were canceled [due to a terror threat.](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/taylor-swift-vienna-terror-plot-third-person-detained-1235750067/) In statement on Aug. 7, 2024, Barracuda Music, the concert promoters for the Austrian shows said, “With confirmation from government officials of a planned terrorist attack at Ernst Happel Stadium, we have no choice but to cancel the three scheduled shows for everyone’s safety. All tickets will be automatically refunded within the next 10 business days.”

Below, check out the list of all the surprise songs she’s brought to The Eras Tour, courtesy of social media livestreams and post-concert clips uploaded by Swifties in attendance. Bookmark this page to “remember this moment” forevermore.

*   “The Best Day”
--------------

_Performed at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (May 14, 2023)_

Tears had to have been aplenty throughout the stadium on Mother’s Day as Swift told the story of “The Best Day” and performed it on piano.

“I secretly recorded a song on _Fearless_,” she told the crowd, recalling being 16 or 17 at the time and explaining that it was very tricky to get this project done without her mother knowing. “It was very sneaky and fun,” she said.

“I wrote this song just compiling these sort of core childhood memories I had of not just her as a mother but her as a friend,” Swift said. After playing the sweet song for her mom for the first time, while showing her the video of personal family footage set to the track that she edited together herself, she asked her mom, “Did you like the song?” “It’s such a beautiful song. Where did you find it? It sounds exactly like the things we went through” Mom replied, not even comprehending that her own daughter would write a song about the two of them. “I wrote it and recorded it secretly,” Taylor told her. “It _is_ our memories. That’s about us.” Needless to say, there were plenty of tears that day, too.

*   “Dear John”
-----------

_Performed at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis (June 24, 2023)_

Swift prefaced her “Dear John” performance by encouraging fans to show “kindness and gentleness” on the internet ahead of her _Speak Now (Taylor’s Version)_ album release on July 7.

“I’m 33 years old. I don’t care about anything that happened to me when I was 19,” she said when introducing the 2010 ballad, about a toxic relationship with an older man, widely assumed to be the singer’s ex-boyfriend[John Mayer](https://www.billboard.com/artist/john-mayer/).

“I’m not putting this album out so that you can go and should feel the need to defend me on the internet against someone you think I might have written a song about 14 billion years ago.”

“Dear John” appears on Swift’s third album,_Speak Now_. The track peaked at No. 54 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in 2010.

*   “Right Where You Left Me”
-------------------------

_Performed at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif. (July 28, 2023)_

Swift teamed up with her frequent collaborator[Aaron Dessner](https://www.billboard.com/artist/aaron-dessner/)for the first live performance of “Right Where You Left Me” in Santa Clara, Calif., on July 28. Prior to the performance, Swift warned concert-goers that it was one of her more challenging songs to play live.

“Because it’s one of our favorites, there’s more pressure on it,” Swift[told](https://youtu.be/Q9hThSaPy24)the crowd. “Also, this is one of the wordiest songs. I have been rehearsing this for weeks, OK? And I’ve never, ever gotten it 100% right. Not even one time. If this is the time that I get it right, you have no idea what kind of celebration I’m going to be exhibiting after that. And also, this goes for you. If you can get all the words right to this song, you get to pat yourself on the back. You win an imaginary prize. It’s yours. We love this song and I hope that I somewhat do it justice.”

As expected, the songstress goofed up the lyrics before laughing it off and starting again where they left off. “It was too good to be true!” she said. “I knew that I would f— that up! We really can’t let that be it, so now we’ve got to go back.”

### Speak Now [Deluxe Edition] Review by Stephen Thomas Erlewine

When [Kanye West](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/kanye-west-mn0000361014) bum-rushed Taylor Swift’s acceptance speech at the 2009 VMAs, the world rallied around Swift not because [Kanye](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/kanye-mn0000361014) was a “jackass,” as [President Obama](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/president-obama-mn0001011538) so succinctly summarized, but because the singer/songwriter conveyed the fragility of adolescence on her 2008 breakthrough, [Fearless](https://www.allmusic.com/album/fearless-mw0000813082), so successfully that she inspired instinctive protectiveness even among those who never spent much time with the record. Not timid or a tart, Swift seemed like a genuine girl on [Fearless](https://www.allmusic.com/album/fearless-mw0000813082), perhaps treating her songs a little too much like diaries, but that only made them more affecting. If anything, Swift ramps up the confessions on her 2010 sequel, Speak Now, but circumstances have changed: few listeners, if any, would have a clue about the identity of the boy who belongs with Taylor, but now that she’s a superstar, anybody with a passing familiarity with pop culture can discern which songs are about [Kanye](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/kanye-mn0000361014), [Taylor Lautner](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/taylor-lautner-mn0002323553) (her ex), or Camilla Belle (the actress girl who stole [Joe Jonas](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/joe-jonas-mn0002622976) out from under our heroine). Not that Swift takes great pains to disguise who she’s writing about -- not when she’s writing “Dear John,” an elegant evisceration of lecherous lothario [John Mayer](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/john-mayer-mn0000239827). Such gossip mongering is titillating but fleeting, suggesting that the charms of Speak Now are insubstantial, but Swift’s gift is that she sets the troubled mind of an awkward age in stone. She writes from the perspective of the moment yet has the skill of a songwriter beyond her years, articulating contradictions and confessions with keen detail and strong melody. Tellingly, underneath all her girlishness -- and Taylor makes no apologies for being girly as she baits mean girls, dreamily thinks of stolen kisses on a sidewalk, or fantasizes about stealing away her ex-lover at the altar -- there’s a steely strength. She walks away proudly from breakups and never dwells on mistakes; she moves forward. The same could be said about the sound of Speak Now itself, which is no great progression from [Fearless](https://www.allmusic.com/album/fearless-mw0000813082) but rather a subtle shift toward pure pop with the country accents, such as the [Dixie Chicks](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/dixie-chicks-mn0000162487) foundation of “Mean,” used as flavoring. But that blend of pop and country, while certainly radio-friendly, is nearly as distinctive to Taylor Swift as her songwriting voice. She may be not a girl, and not yet a woman, but on Speak Now she captures that transition with a personal grace and skill that few singer/songwriters have. [A Deluxe CD/DVD version was also released.]

Taylor Swift: Birthday Girl, By-The-Numbers

“I’m so 22 right now,” birthday girl Taylor Swift Tweeted this morning (Dec. 13).

In honor of her special day, Chart Beat spotlights a host of the chart records that Billboard’s 2011 Woman of the Year and the top [country](https://www.billboard.com/t/country/) artist of the past 12 months has achieved, all since her arrival just more than five years ago.

**HER ‘SONG’S:** Swift is the **only female artist to collect five top 10s from a debut album in the 68-year history of Hot Country Songs.**

### Explore

[![Image 7: A blonde woman in a denim dress and jacket, looking into the distance, is standing in front of a doorway](https://charts-static.billboard.com/img/2005/04/carrie-underwood-dzv-344x344.jpg)](https://www.billboard.com/artist/carrie-underwood/)

### [Carrie Underwood](https://www.billboard.com/artist/carrie-underwood/)

[![Image 8: Faith Hill is smiling in a portrait with long blond hair](https://charts-static.billboard.com/img/1993/10/faith-hill-n2i-344x344.jpg)](https://www.billboard.com/artist/faith-hill/)

### [Faith Hill](https://www.billboard.com/artist/faith-hill/)

[![Image 9: Taylor Swift smiles with the wind in her hair and seagulls in the background](https://charts-static.billboard.com/img/2006/07/taylor-swift-vug-344x344.jpg)](https://www.billboard.com/artist/taylor-swift/)

### [Taylor Swift](https://www.billboard.com/artist/taylor-swift/)

See latest videos, charts and news

Here is a look at the Hot Country Songs chart performance of the five singles from “Taylor Swift,” which entered the Billboard 200 the week of Nov. 11, 2006. The set’s 249 weeks on the tally are the most by an album in the 2000s:

### Related

[![Image 10: Rufus Wainwright](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/rufus-wainwright-2025-new-yorker-festival-billboard-1800.jpg?w=237&h=147&crop=1) ### Rufus Wainwright, Lucius & Lord Huron Added to L.A. Wildfire Anniversary Benefit Concert](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/rufus-wainwright-lucius-lord-huron-la-wildfire-benefit-show-1236143842/)

[![Image 11: Lily Allen, Lola Young and Olivia Rodrigo](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/lily-allen-lola-young-olivia-rodrigo-2025-billboard-1800.jpg?w=237&h=147&crop=1) ### Lola Young Makes First Public Appearance Since Onstage Collapse at Lily Allen's Holiday Party](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/lola-young-first-public-appearance-onstage-collapse-1236143835/)

[![Image 12: Rauw Alejandro](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/01-Rauw-Alejandro-25-live-billboard-1800.jpg?w=237&h=147&crop=1) ### Rauw Alejandro's Free Concert in Dominican Republic & More Uplifting Moments in Latin Music](https://www.billboard.com/music/latin/rauw-alejandro-free-concert-latin-music-uplifting-moments-1236142467/)

Peak Position, Title, Peak Year

 No. 6, “Tim McGraw,” 2007

 No. 2, “Teardrops on My Guitar,” 2007

 No. 1 (six weeks), “Our Song,” 2007-08

 No. 3, “Picture to Burn,” 2008

 No. 1 (two weeks), “Should’ve Said No,” 2007-08

With the six-week reign of “Our Song,” Swift joined just four other women who have claimed such lengthy stays on top: Kitty Wells (“It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels,” six weeks, 1952); Connie Smith (“Once a Day,” eight, 1964); Faith Hill (“Breathe,” six, 2000); and, Carrie Underwood (“Jesus, Take the Wheel,” six, 2006).

**MORE TO THE ‘STORY’:** Swift followed the unprecedented success of her first album’s singles on Hot Country Songs by becoming the **first woman to bank five top 10s from each of her first two studio sets.**

In the chart’s archives, only two other acts have racked five top 10s from each of their first two releases: Brooks & Dunn notched five top 10s each from “Brand New Man” and “Hard Workin’ Man” (1991-94) and Dixie Chicks hatched five top 10s from their major label debut “Wide Open Spaces” and six from “Fly” (1998-2002).

Here is a look at how the five songs promoted to [radio](https://www.billboard.com/t/radio/) from Swift’s sophomore album “Fearless” fared on Hot Country Songs:

Peak Position, Title, Peak Year

 No. 1 (two weeks), “Love Story,” 2008

 No. 2, “White Horse,” 2009

 No. 1 (two weeks), “You Belong With Me,” 2009

 No. 7, “Fifteen,” 2009

 No. 10, “Fearless,” 2010

**‘BACK’ AGAIN:** The four singles from Swift’s third full-length album “Speak Now,” Billboard’s No. 1 country album of 2011, all reached the Hot Country Songs top 10: “Mine” (No. 2), “Back to December” (No. 3), “Mean” (No. 2) and “Sparks Fly” (No. 1, one week).

As all 14 of her promoted (non-seasonal) radio cuts have reached the top bracket, Swift and Carrie Underwood are tied for the **best career-opening top 10 streak among women in the chart’s archives.**

Can her new single, “Ours,” push her into the lead? The song, from Swift’s “Speak Now: World Tour Live” CD/DVD, is off to a strong start, zooming 37-28 in its third chart week.

**UP WHERE SHE ‘BELONG’S:** After becoming the first country artist to win a Moonman at the MTV Video Music Awards, Swift likewise broke barriers on Billboard’s Hot 100 Airplay survey.

On the Oct. 3, 2009, chart, “You Belong With Me” rose 2-1 to become the **first country crossover No. 1** since the list adopted Nielsen BDS-monitored data in 1990.

Previously among country singles, Shania Twain’s “You’re Still the One” (1998), Faith Hill’s “Breathe” (2000) and Swift’s own “Love Story” (March 2009) had each peaked as high as No. 2 on Hot 100 Airplay.

**‘FEARLESS’ IS MORE:** With 11 weeks logged at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 album chart between November 2008 and March 2009, “Fearless” is **one of just eight albums by women to rule for such a length** in the ranking’s 55-year history:

Weeks at No. 1, Artist, Title, Peak Year

 20, Whitney Houston, “The Bodyguard” soundtrack, 1992

 15, Carole King, “Tapestry,” 1971

 14, Whitney Houston, “Whitney Houston,” 1986

 13, Adele, “21,” 2011

 13, Judy Garland, “Judy at Carnegie Hall,” 1961

 12, Alanis Morissette, “Jagged Little Pill,” 1995

**11, Taylor Swift, “Fearless,” 2008**

 11, Mariah Carey, “Mariah Carey,” 1991

**SWIFT STARTS:** When “If This Was a Movie” debuted at No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 last month, Swift extended her mark for the **most top 10 launches in the chart’s 52-year ledger.**

In October 2010, “Speak Now” (No. 8) and “Back to December” (No. 6) debuted in the top tier in back-to-back weeks, making Swift the first artist ever to begin in the Hot 100’s top 10 in consecutive weeks.

Here is a recap of the acts with the most top 10 Hot 100 entrances:

 6, Lil Wayne

 5, Mariah Carey

 5, Eminem

 4, the Beatles

 4, Miley Cyrus/Hannah Montana

 4, Janet Jackson

 4, Lady Gaga
